knowledge.statement: When readOnly.recvAck is given an 8-byte Context value larger than the number of outstanding read requests, the ReadOnlySafe confirmation path behaves as follows in this snapshot. With a quorum of such values (leader self-ack position 1 plus two peers at position 2^40, voters {1,2,3}), readOnly.maybeAdvance panics inside its slice expression: 'runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:1099511627776] with capacity 1'. With a single such value (two admitted reads, leader self-ack position 2, an honest peer at position 1, one peer at position 2 that received no heartbeat carrying position 2), maybeAdvance does not panic and instead returns both admitted reads (advanced=2, confirmed_reads=2), i.e. it confirms a read index that the forged voter never observed. Both outcomes were observed with the ack map, unconfirmedReads and confirmedReads driven directly; no raft instance, network or storage was involved.
knowledge.conditions: ReadOnlySafe; ack values are injected directly into the unexported readOnly via recvAck instead of being produced by the library's follower path (handleHeartbeat), which is the out-of-contract premise. Quorum position is the median of stored acks because CommittedIndex is evaluated over quorum.JointConfig{1,2,3},nil. Does not apply to ReadOnlyLeaseBased, which does not use the ack map.

knowledge.assertion: with a quorum of oversized ack values maybeAdvance panics; with a single forged value it confirms reads the voter never observed
recvAck stores the peer Context as a raw read position and maybeAdvance slices unconfirmedReads by the quorum position without validating the value
every legal Context producer echoes the live leader's emitted value, so the out-of-range precondition has no in-model trigger

interpretations.rationale: Measured interpretation of the revised fixed experiment, superseding the conditional account written against the first receipt. Receipt 8dd8fb7e47a14057ba98a6755fdc5b49 (experiment cbcc326c8c1b40b8beafb5b33802bddf-experiment) ran in the isolated workspace with -run ^TestAssurance; status completed, outcome tests_passed, exit 0, empty stderr, no changed target files, no parsing errors. Decisive parsed indices and their admissions: index 0 is the oversized-case admission (read_requests=1, leader_ack_position=1, forged_ack_position=2^40, voters 1,2,3) and index 1 its result (panicked=true, panic text 'runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:1099511627776] with capacity 1'); index 2 is the forged-case admission (read_requests=2, leader_ack_position=2, honest_ack_position=1, forged_ack_position=2) and index 3 its result (advanced=2, confirmed_reads=2). The controller recorded outcome holds for both declared comparisons, each correlated against its own admission (comparison 0 -> prerequisite index 0, comparison 1 -> prerequisite index 2) with comparison_complete=true and no missing indices or diagnostics; the earlier unknown outcome was caused by my duplicate event names and is fixed by this revision, which changes only event naming, not the target, prefix or assertions. What this establishes: under an out-of-contract Context the ReadOnlySafe confirmation path either exceeds the unconfirmedReads slice bound and panics, or confirms a read that the supplying voter never observed, exactly as the source reading predicted. What it does not establish, and therefore what keeps the defect claim refuted: the experiment supplies those ack values itself, so no observation here bears on whether a legal producer can deliver a Context the live instance never emitted. That question was answered separately by source enumeration (a167f4c33dc94f34b03ea29dbe7ec15a-knowledge-0: readOnly is created only by raft.reset at a leadership transition, handleHeartbeat is the sole writer of MsgHeartbeatResp.Context and echoes the leader's value, lower-term responses are dropped before dispatch, and heartbeatCtx emits a message total that path only grows), so the condition remains a fault-model violation rather than an in-model consensus defect. Unchanged uncertainty, still unclaimed: addRequest does not deduplicate by request context, so documented ReadIndex retries with an identical context accumulate one unconfirmed entry and one heartbeat broadcast each while the leader cannot reach a quorum ack; I have not established that this is reportable.
limitations: The experiment injects ack values directly into the unexported readOnly, so the holds result characterises the confirmation path under an out-of-contract input and establishes no network reachability.
The in-model premise refutation (no legal producer of an un-emitted Context) is still a source argument; two executions in this run tested the consequence, not the premise.

The panic outcome shares the same missing bound as the premature-confirmation outcome; a fix would need to bound the stored ack against the outstanding request count, which this run does not investigate.
